source.title: Parle: parallelizing stochastic gradient descent
source.authors: Pratik Chaudhari; Carlo Baldassi; R. Zecchina; Stefano Soatto; A. Talwalkar; Adam M. Oberman

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training and validation error and argues Parle can improve validation performance at the cost of higher training error, qualifying the generalization-gap claim in particular settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out validation and training errors for several methods and datasets. Rows below include those reported separately in tables and text; graph-only training-error comparisons are described textually without assigning unmarked curve values. Cited prior-work results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flat minima improve generalization to design Parle and reports its performance. It tests none of V1–V8: in particular, it neither measures magnitude-aware sharpness nor compares generalization-measure rankings, and its optimizer comparisons do not involve adaptive methods.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as a summary of the authors' interpretation. They conclude that Parle improves benchmark validation performance over SGD with the same architecture and attribute this to seeking flat regions, sometimes at the cost of underfitting. Their experiments do not directly measure flatness, and the validation advantage does not hold on SVHN.
record.recipe_differences: Parle is a new parallel training algorithm combining local-entropy updates with elastic coupling and scoping. The paper reports comparison methods, not the claim versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Number of replicas changes performance: with n=8, CIFAR networks show an initial speedup but converge to worse error than n=3 under the same hyperparameters. On SVHN, Elastic-SGD with scoping reaches 1.57%, while without scoping the paper reports no errors below 1.9%. Training and validation error profiles also vary by algorithm.

fits_no_version.finding: Parle lowers validation error relative to SGD on CIFAR-10 from 4.29% to 3.24% and on CIFAR-100 from 18.85% to 17.64%, while retaining higher training error. On SVHN, its 1.68% validation error is comparable to SGD's 1.62%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local-entropy training with coupled replicas can improve held-out performance while fitting training data less closely, with benefits depending on the dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Parle achieves 5.89% and 6.08% validation error when replicas individually access 50% and 25% of CIFAR-10, respectively, versus 6.15% for full-data SGD; the replica subsets collectively retain all examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coupled replicas can learn effectively from overlapping data subsets whose union covers the full training set.

record.problems: Some comparisons report results from a single run rather than three; the authors explicitly note this for some networks. Several plotted training-error trajectories have no fully recoverable per-method numeric values in the supplied text. These experiments compare Parle and SGD, not arbitrary-label memorization or the claim versions' specified mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: Training-error curves in Figure 5 are summarized by the text as near-zero for SGD and Elastic-SGD and larger for Entropy-SGD and Parle; no extra numerical rows were extracted because the supplied figure text does not map all displayed values reliably to methods. Figure-only validation curves not additionally transcribed where corresponding table values exist.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under limited or broader tuning.
No batch-size intervention under fixed epoch budgets; large-batch findings are discussed from prior work.
Dropout is used but its contribution is not isolated or varied.
No magnitude-scaled perturbation measurement, correlation with generalization gaps, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. Flatness is a design premise rather than a measured result.
No memorization-based example selection or comparison of targeted and random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Higher training error alongside lower validation error does not qualify any stated version by itself. All extracted rows report the proposed method's performance or its comparators and should remain outside version-specific evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Dropout is present in some setups, but its effect is not tested by adding/removing or varying dropout.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.
